minimal_context: The student is participating in a build-to-play group session using LEGO and magnetic vehicles.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our build-to-play group session. Let's use these LEGOs and magnetic vehicles to build something together.

STUDENT: (Singing in a high-pitched, changed voice) I am the boss of the building! Give me all the pieces right now!

TUTOR: Let's just share the pieces with the other children.

STUDENT: (Reaches across the table, crossing boundaries to grab another child's magnetic vehicles) No, they are doing it wrong! I need them!

TUTOR: Please stay in your spot and keep building your own tower.

STUDENT: You are stupid! It's your fault it's ruined! (Throws the magnetic vehicles across the table)

options.A: Make the student aware that their goal during the 14 build-to-play sessions is not just to finish building by themselves, but to ensure that the whole group completes the task.
options.B: Follow a structured plan across the 14 build-to-play sessions, divided into four stages: Stage 1 for rapport building, Stage 2 for practicing positive social skills, Stage 3 for setting boundaries, and Stage 4 for termination.
options.C: Ask the student what they think went wrong with the LEGOs and magnetic vehicles during the 14 build-to-play sessions, instead of simply telling them what went wrong.
options.D: Provide follow-in talk related to the student's ongoing actions and attention throughout the 14 build-to-play sessions, focusing on their immediate use of the LEGOs and magnetic vehicles.
